key_insight: A reduced gas-dynamic model captures post-pulse gas expansion far more accurately than existing global-model closures while running roughly 1,000 times faster than CFD.
engineering_relevance: Accurate expansion modeling improves predictions of gas density, heating and dissociation in nanosecond pulsed discharges, especially during high-frequency operation.
method: Represent the expanding gas with Lagrangian shells.
Close the model with an approximate cylindrical acoustic radiation condition and no fitted physical coefficient.
Couple gas dynamics to the SoPlasma-0D plasma-kinetics solver.
evidence_signal: Against verified 1D compressible CFD, axis-density errors stayed within 2.4% for smooth deposition profiles and axis pressures up to six times ambient; existing closures overpredicted density by up to 2.8× relative to the coupled model two microseconds after a single pulse.
watch_item: The reported accuracy is established for smooth deposition profiles in a cylindrical expansion framework; performance outside the tested regimes needs validation.
paper_title: Gas expansion in global models of nanosecond pulsed discharges: a reduced gas-dynamic model coupled to plasma kinetics
